transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-08
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Riley (Redwood SE), Priya (Horizon PM), Marcus (Horizon ML Eng), Sofia (Horizon Sec)

Summary: quick demo of Console + Optimize features that matter for Horizon's prompt quality pipeline; include sample A/B compare and regression alert configuration.

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Alex on AE, Riley SE, and we heard from Priya earlier about the need for prompt monitoring across your chat flows. How's everyone doing?

[00:12] Priya: Good thanks, yeah excited to see how this can fit into our release. we have a few pain points: drifting prompts, customer escalations when answers change, and cost spikes when we switch models.

[00:25] Marcus: Hi, Marcus here — real quick, we run on a hybrid infra, some requests go to our on-prem GPU pool, others to cloud. latency needs to be <350ms p95 for chat, and we need to capture telemetry for each prompt.

[00:40] Riley: Great, we'll try to hit those. today's demo shows the Console's prompt-sets feature, the regression alerts, and the A/B comparison — plus some notes on routing between Hosted and Dedicated. I'll share my screen now.

[01:02] [screen share starts — brief silence as people load the dashboard]

[01:18] Riley: Ok so this is the Evalops console — apologies if the name looks slightly different, sometimes our internal labels render as 'Eval-ops' in the UI. On the left is Prompt Library, middle is Runs and Ab-Compare, right is Alerts. We'll open a sample prompt-set we created from the sample data you sent.

[01:36] Marcus: Wait that sample — is that the 1k prompt batch we uploaded last week? I think a few of the IDs got changed.

[01:44] Alex: Yeah we normalized them, some ids got sanitized. you'll still see original text in the prompt field.

[01:52] Riley: Here we have Prompt-Set: 'horizon-chat-1k', each prompt is tagged with intent, expected answer, and a quality rubric. You can add variants for A/B testing: v1 uses the Redwood-hosted Llama2-Chat-70b-v3 and v2 uses a quantized 8-bit Optimized variant.

[02:15] Priya: So we can compare quality and cost side-by-side? like a cost per correct response metric?

[02:22] Riley: Exactly. in the A/B compare view you pick the prompt-set and the two model variants or routing policies. you get token-level cost, p95 latency, top-level quality metrics (exact-match, rubric average), and more human-centric metrics like helpfulness and hallucination rate if you supply labels.

[02:44] [02:44] Marcus: How are hallucinations measured? we have different definitions across teams.

[02:51] Riley: We support custom evaluation scripts and pairwise human labels. you can upload a rubric csv or use the built-in heuristics — e.g., entity-mismatch and hallucination keywords. for production we recommend mixing automated heuristics with spot human labels to calibrate thresholds.

[03:10] Sofia: From a security perspective, the console stores prompt texts in logs for evaluation — how long do those persist and can we encrypt them with our keys?

[03:22] Alex: good question. we have retention controls per project and full KMS integration for Private deployments; Hosted has managed keys but you can opt into BYOK via our Dedicated or Private plans. retention settings can be set to 30/90/365 days or disabled for sensitive collections.

[03:40] Sofia: Is audit logging exportable to our SIEM?

[03:45] Riley: yes — audit logs and token traces are exportable to your S3 or to our syslog endpoint; we can stream alerts to your pagerduty as well. we'll attach the security pack with exact endpoints.

[03:58] Priya: back to the A/B compare — can we run a split test by routing policy instead of model? like send 10% to Dedicated and 90% to Hosted?

[04:12] Riley: Absolutely. The routing abstraction lets you compare policies: you can route by tag, user tier, region, or percentage splits. the A/B analysis will show per-route metrics. that's useful for cost-latency tradeoffs.

[04:36] [04:36] Marcus: For our baseline, p95 needs to be under 350ms — how do we set SLO alerts?

[04:44] Riley: In Alerts, create a new regression alert: pick metric p95 latency, scope to the prompt-set or route, set baseline window and alert threshold e.g., 350ms, and then set cooldown and severity. we also support anomaly detection — the system will suggest thresholds based on historical distribution.

[05:06] Priya: If we roll out a new prompt edit and it triggers an alert, can we auto-rollback to the previous prompt variant?

[05:15] Riley: Yes, with our rollout policies you can configure auto-fallback: if quality or latency regresses beyond thresholds, traffic is automatically shifted back to the previous variant and we create an incident with the diff of prompt changes.

[05:32] Alex: quick note — diffs show the prompt text changes and a side-by-side metric delta which is handy for RCA.

[05:40] [05:40] Marcus: Sounds great. about the metric calculations: are token costs normalized across models? we use per-token costs that differ by model family.

[05:50] Riley: Costs are normalized to a USD per-token view using your billing rates; for Dedicated we'll use the committed GPU-based rate you choose. Console will show both raw token counts and estimated cost so you can decide.

[06:05] Priya: Can you demo a regression alert firing?

[06:10] Riley: Sure — I'll fire a synthetic run. I'm going to push a deliberate prompt variant that adds an ambiguous context, run the A/B compare, and we'll watch the alert engine.

[06:24] [06:24] Riley executes a test; the dashboard refreshes

[06:32] Riley: ok, see here — the hallucination heuristic jumped from 4% to 18% on v2, p95 latency increased to 420ms, cost per call up 35% — the alert rule triggered and created an incident with recommended rollback.

[06:50] Priya: I'm seeing the incident email — it includes sample responses?

[06:54] Riley: It includes anonymized transcripts and the examples that violated the rubric. full examples are available in the prompt run logs if you have permission.

[07:06] Sofia: Permissioning, yes — do we have RBAC on who can see raw PII in prompts?

[07:12] Alex: we support role-based access controls, field-level redaction, and project scoping. you can mask specific fields before they persist to logs. we'll include a config snippet in the security docs.

[07:28] Marcus: Ok, two follow-ups: 1) we want to run a 1-week pilot using our sample prompts and compare the current model to a quantized variant and 2) we want sampling of human labels for 200 examples across worst-performing prompts. can Redwood help instrument that?

[07:45] Alex: yes — pilot is the typical path. we can set up a Dedicated pool for the pilot or use Hosted with a routing rule. we'll capture telemetry, run A/B splits, and provide evaluation dashboards.

[08:00] Riley: For human labels, we have an integration with third-party labelers or you can upload CSVs. the Console shows labeling progress and feeds it back into the quality metrics.

[08:12] Priya: How do we onboard prompts? is there an API? we have CI that pushes prompt changes from a git repo.

[08:20] Riley: There's a Prompt Sets API — you can push versioned prompt-json and metadata. The Console also supports a Git-backed flow: each PR can trigger a dry-run evaluation and a diff in the UI.

[08:34] Marcus: That git integration is critical for us — want to prevent accidental prompt drift in prod.

[08:40] Alex: We'll show the repo flow in the pilot.

[08:45] [08:45] Priya: On compliance, earlier we talked about data residency. our EU customers need prompt logs to remain in the eu-west region. is that possible on Hosted?

[08:55] Riley: Hosted has region controls; we can pin projects to region endpoints. for stricter needs we recommend Private with VPC peering or Dedicated in your cloud account.

[09:08] Sofia: Also need to confirm that we can rotate keys and bring our own KMS for encryption at rest.

[09:14] Alex: Affirmative. BYOK is supported in Dedicated/Private and we'll include HSM options in the security pack.

[09:24] [09:24] Marcus: A couple of nitty-gritty questions: how are KV cache effects considered in A/B tests? e.g., if v1 benefits from cached context and v2 doesn't, could that skew latency?

[09:35] Riley: Good call — the run engine can control cache-warming and clear cache between runs to ensure fair comparisons. we also expose per-query cache-hit stats so you can normalize metrics.

[09:48] Priya: What about reranking and embeddings — can we include those downstream steps in the metric pipeline?

[09:55] Riley: Yes, you can instrument multi-step flows and tag per-step metrics: embedding latency, reranker precision, final answer quality. The A/B compare supports composite pipelines.

[10:10] [10:10] Alex: Let's talk about timelines — if Horizon signs pilot this week, we can spin up the pilot env in 3 business days and start ingesting prompts. after 7 days we'll run a full AB analysis and deliver a recommendation.

[10:26] Priya: Sounds reasonable. budget wise, can you estimate cost for the pilot? we want a ballpark for Dedicated vs Hosted.

[10:34] Alex: We'll send a pilot quote — Hosted pricing is usage-based; Dedicated is a reserved monthly commit. for a 1-week pilot with 100k tokens/day, Hosted is likely in the low thousands USD; Dedicated pricing depends on GPU type — we'll provide a few options.

[10:52] Marcus: Any vendor lock-in — if we want to export all metrics and stop, can we?

[10:59] Riley: Yes exports are supported for both metrics and raw logs. we can provide JSON exports or a direct S3 export.

[11:08] Priya: Who should be our point of contact to get the security docs and pilot contract?

[11:12] Alex: Riley will send the security pack; I'll send the pilot agreement and pricing. I'll be your AE and coordinate.

[11:20] Sofia: Quick question — do you have SI keyboards — I mean SIEM connectors?

[11:25] Riley: yes — syslog, S3, and semantic SIEM connectors, we'll include connector docs.

[11:32] [11:32] Priya: ok let's summarize next steps. Riley to send security pack and SOC2; Alex to send pilot pricing and contract; Marcus to share the 1k prompt set and confirm the 200 examples for human labeling. schedule pilot kickoff next week pending availability.

[11:52] [closing] Alex: Thank you all. we'll follow up with the artifacts.

[End of transcript]

Notes on transcription quality: medium — some proper nouns may be off (e.g., 'Evalops' vs 'Eval Ops'), occasional word swaps and stutters.
